hook: Your AI product can be useful today and become someone else’s bundled feature tomorrow.
readerPromise: Examine a conditional investment thesis about where durable bargaining power might remain as AI capabilities become widely rentable.
protectedRevelations: Specific portfolio targets, underwriting prescriptions and final investment recommendations
visualPlan: A useful product can disappear: Show a useful independent AI product appear as one feature inside a larger suite. Keep the independent team beside a lasting customer need that survives the change in interface.
What can a company retain?: Place two teams using similar models beside different records, services and responsibilities.
When control points move: Show a short sequence of computing tools with the control point changing between them.
Beyond the demonstration: Keep a polished demonstration separate from the ownership and service dependencies it needs.
What repeated work builds: Let completed work add to a reusable case record rather than a rising-profit graph.
A wager that can fail: Place the proposed strategy beside a failed trial and its retained lesson.
Follow the claim on value: End on the useful output and the unanswered question of who can retain its value.

cueChanges.nextVisualChange: Retain the independent tool and suite comparison with no invented market winner.
Keep the reusable evaluation artifact as a question about what survives, not a measured advantage.
Use one changing platform control point, simplifying component-switch demonstrations.
Keep review, authority and relationship objects visibly distinct.
Show a repeated deployment leaving a reusable record without promising compounding returns.
Preserve the failed-trial record and next decision as open possibilities.
End on the actual thesis with the opening value question still visible.

authorReview.scope: Complete eight-sentence script checked against canonical short-reader opening evidence for premise, clear identity, specific interest and protected revelations.
authorReview.targetDuration: About one minute at an unhurried conversational pace with real pauses; measure after recording.
authorReview.emotion: Concrete recognition, thoughtful tension and open curiosity; no melodramatic mystery or inflated promise.
authorReview.audioConversion: Blocked until all batch scripts pass independent editorial review.
authorReview.visualExecution: The existing art is preserved as working material; book-specific changes above still require implementation before film validation.

independentReview.notes: Every spoken sentence reviewed against canonical English short reader for clear newcomer meaning, source grounding, curiosity and emotional intent. Replaced abstract promotional commentary with concrete viewer-facing language. All eight sentences have a distinct intended response and explicit restrained TTS direction; fictional later outcomes remain withheld. This is editorial review, not audience testing or rendered-audio approval. Reopened for the distinctive-contribution pass: concrete premises retained for fiction; proposed concepts, architectures and controversial positions now appear early where relevant. No unsupported world-first claim is made.

sentenceIntentions.text: Your AI product can be useful today and become someone else’s bundled feature tomorrow.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Show a useful AI product vulnerable to absorption
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Recognize the gap between demand and durable advantage

sentenceIntentions.text: Investing in an AI-Dominated Economy proposes building around lasting needs that cheaper AI makes more important.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: State the proposed investment direction rather than only its genre
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand the conditional focus on needs made more important by cheaper AI

sentenceIntentions.text: It asks what a company can keep building when capable models become widely available to competitors.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Ask what remains when capable models are widely rentable
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Become curious about defensible sources of value

sentenceIntentions.text: The book looks back at computing history to ask who gained power when new tools became widely available.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Follow changing control points across computing eras
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Expect historical mechanisms rather than guaranteed forecasts

sentenceIntentions.text: A convincing demonstration says little about who controls the evidence, relationships, and services the product needs.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Separate ownership and relationships from demonstration quality
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Question what an impressive product actually controls

sentenceIntentions.text: It explores how repeated work might become skills and institutions a company can build on.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Connect repeated work with institutional capability
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: See a longer horizon than one successful feature

sentenceIntentions.text: The strategy is a bet with stated assumptions, including reasons it might fail.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Keep the strategy a wager with failure conditions
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand that the reading invites scrutiny rather than certainty

sentenceIntentions.text: Begin with the difference between creating value and having a durable claim on it.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Start from creating value versus retaining a claim
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Want to examine where future bargaining power may reside

distinctiveContribution: A proposed venture-studio strategy separates useful AI products from enduring claims on value when underlying cognitive capability becomes widely available.
